crop.notes: Headline 'How an Irishman Won a Ring Title for United States' through the closing quote; nothing cut off.

summary.suggested: The New St. Louis Star printed Bill Clark's account of how the ring championship came to America, recalling Allen's arrest in England before a planned Goss fight, his 1867 arrival and his fights with McCoole and Goss.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'New St. Louis Star, Tuesday Evening, March 17, 1914', page 11. By Billy Murphy, from Prof. Bill Clark. The current summary wrongly calls McCoole British.

facts.fact: Before leaving England, Allen and Joe Goss signed articles to fight for the English championship, but both were arrested on bench warrants on the eve of the fight
Allen came to America in 1867 with other English pugilists, then about 5 feet 10 inches and 164 pounds
Clark said that in Allen's fight with Mike McCoole, McCoole's friends stopped the fight with gunfire when Allen was winning
Clark said Allen and Goss fought for the championship of the world in America, and Goss's armed backers forced the referee to decide for Goss when he was losing

notes: Most of the article is about Paddy Ryan, Goss and Sullivan; Allen is in the first half. Clark's account of the McCoole fight is a loose recollection; the fight is not dated in the text (dates on facts are inferred).
